title: Someone is inside your home
lede: It is 3am. Downstairs there is a sound that is not the house — a click, a footstep, a door moving. You are fully awake and your heart is loud enough to hear.

blocks.text: It is 3am. Downstairs there is a sound that is not the house — a click, a footstep, a door moving. You are fully awake and your heart is loud enough to hear.

items: Every object in your home is insured or replaceable. You are not. Confronting an intruder over property is the highest-cost, lowest-return decision available.
Most burglars want absence, not conflict. Signalling that the house is awake and observed ends most events immediately.
You have two real options: get out, or barricade and call. Which one depends on whether the exit route is clear of them and whether others in the house are with you or elsewhere.

items.move: Do not announce yourself by going to look
items.detail: Investigating means walking toward the danger with no plan and no light.

items.move: If your exit is clear, leave immediately
items.detail: Out and to a neighbour. Do not gather belongings. Do not get dressed properly.

items.move: If it is not clear, lock yourself in with the others
items.detail: Best room with a solid door. Furniture against it. Everyone in one place — never split a household in a live intrusion.

items.move: Call emergency services and stay on the line
items.detail: Whisper if needed. Give the address first, always, before anything else — if the call drops, the address is what brings help.
Lights on, an alarm, the car key fob to set off the car horn from upstairs. Noise and light evict most intruders in seconds.
Never block an exit route. A trapped intruder becomes a violent one. Property leaving the house is a good outcome.

items.say: "14 Oakfield Road, flat 2. Someone is in my house. I am upstairs with my daughter, door locked."

items.when: Through the door, if it forces the issue
items.say: Loud: "Police are on the way." Not a threat, a fact, and usually sufficient.
"Stay next to me, stay quiet, we are safe in here and help is coming." Calm voice. They will take their state from yours.

items: Going downstairs to check. This is the decision that converts burglaries into assaults.
Arming yourself and hunting. Escalates enormously, and in many places creates legal jeopardy for you.
Hanging up to text people. Stay on the line with the service that is sending help.
Blocking the front door or the stairs. Give them the route out.
Do not tidy. It is a crime scene and disturbance destroys evidence.
Photograph everything before touching it, for the report and the insurers.
Change locks the same day, and audit what keys and documents left the house — identity material matters more than electronics.
Do not sleep there alone the first night if you can avoid it. Ask someone to stay.
Expect the fear to arrive properly a day or two later, and expect it to fade. If it does not in a few weeks, talk to someone qualified.

limit: If you are discovered, do not fight over objects. Comply, stay passive, give them what they ask for, keep your hands visible, and put distance and doors between you at the first opportunity. Memorise details only if it is safe to — nothing is worth being hurt for.
